title: Lens and perspective correction
objective: Deliver offline Lensfun v0.3.4 rectilinear profile distortion and manual two-axis perspective through one fused, exactly bounded warp resample, preserving content coordinates, immutable history and exact export while refusing duplicate embedded DNG correction.
context_summary: Functional implementation and native integration are complete. Native performance measurement, the full tier and photographic accuracy qualification remain incomplete. docs/design/lens-and-perspective.md is prescriptive: owner decisions of 2026-09-30 (RAW mosaics without a luminance warp are known-unapplied; Perspective is not presettable; combined minification above 1.8x is refused) and recorded defaults (the index is a separate bundled resource parsed once off the owner; no X100VI alias). Coverage, cover scales and read rectangles are closed forms; the index is a static resource with synchronous lookups; lens, perspective and a straightened crop fuse into one resample; the DNG ledger is derived per plane and never persisted. Wave 1 (numerics, index import, optics ledger, affine refactor, query-choice control) can land any time; the warp-chain and render tasks rebase on Detail's host contracts if those land first; shared generated files are regenerated after each rebase, never hand-merged; timing runs only in TASK-015 after all feature work. Run at most four implementation agents at once. Photographic qualification needs owner-supplied photographs and stays incomplete without them. The owner's decisions of 2026-10-01 shape the Lens section: no list of lenses (the applied or detected profile as a card, a search of compatible profiles only and a prefilled missing-lens report), a new RAW or DNG whose distortion is known uncorrected gets its eligible detected profile as an ordinary system entry after its Original (a JPEG is offered Apply instead), and a curated DJI product-name table for display and reports.

tasks.description: Freeze the lens and perspective numerics in an independent f64 reference and its committed fixture.
extra_context: New files: crates/luxforge-reference/src/geometry.rs (add `pub mod geometry;` to src/lib.rs), crates/luxforge-reference/tests/studies/geometry.rs (add `mod geometry;` to tests/studies/main.rs), fixtures/geometry/lens-perspective.json and fixtures/geometry/README.md. The reference crate imports no product crate.

Functions in geometry.rs, each a transcription of the cited v0.3.4 lines or of the design's closed forms: `lensfun_norm(width, height, crop_lens, crop_camera, aspect_lens) -> f64` (NS, modifier.cpp 203-253), `unit_scale`, `radial_f`, `radial_df`, `radial_inverse_bracketed(model, terms, r_d, r_mono) -> Result<(f64, u32), Outcome>` with `Outcome::{Outside, Unconverged}`, `hermite` (auxfun.cpp 441-462), `lensfun_interpolate(calibrations, focal) -> Result<[f64; 3], Refusal>` (lens.cpp 870-943 plus the design's tolerances), `perspective_forward`, `perspective_inverse`, `cover_scale_lens`, `cover_scale_perspective`, `local_scale_lens`, `local_scale_perspective_bound`, `reads_radial_rect` and `bilinear_linear` (four-tap linear-light sampling of an f64 frame).

Coefficients of the named records are copied from the v0.3.4 XML into geometry.rs as constants, each with its file and line: NIKKOR Z 24-70mm f/4 S (mil-nikon.xml), FC3411 & compatibles (actioncams.xml), X100V & compatibles (Standard), Canon PowerShot G12 & compatibles (Standard) poly5, Olympus M.Zuiko Digital 14-42mm poly3 at 14, Sony E 10-18mm f/4 OSS at 10, Sigma 17-50mm f/2.8 EX DC HSM at 17, Tokina 11-16mm at 11, and one all-zero calibration. Fetch the tag with `git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.3.4 https://github.com/lensfun/lensfun`.

The minification limit (1.8) is an owner decision: this task reports alias energy for a zone plate and a checkerboard at local scales 1.0 to 2.6 in steps of 0.1 into the fixture, and records any finding that contradicts the limit in the design's Coverage section as a question for the owner, never by changing the limit.

`committed_geometry_fixtures_are_current` fails on a stale fixture; `regenerate_committed_geometry_fixtures` is `#[ignore]` and rewrites it, following the vignette study's pattern. The `geometry` filter matches nothing until this task adds the tests.

acceptance_criteria: `lensfun_interpolation_matches_reference_vectors` reproduces the pinned 26/30/42/60 mm terms within 1e-6 and returns the exact calibration at 24, 28, 35, 50 and 70 mm.

`lens_cover_scale_closed_form_matches_dense_sampling` agrees with a 4096-point boundary and 256x256 interior dense check within 1e-9 for every named calibration on 3:2, 4:3 and 1:1 stages, and `barrel_profile_certifies_at_unit_scale` returns exactly 1 for a barrel calibration touching the short-edge midpoint.

`perspective_cover_scale_is_tight_at_extremes`: at s_P every output corner maps inside the input rectangle and at s_P*(1-1e-6) one does not, on 3:2, 4:3, 16:9, 1:1 and 2:3 at Horizontal and Vertical in {-100, 0, 100}.

`perspective_carry_conjugates_all_eight_orientations` reproduces the design's table for (40, -25) and maps 10,000 points through orientation-then-perspective and carried-perspective-then-orientation within 1e-9 px; `lens_map_is_orientation_invariant` does the same for the lens with no payload change.

`lens_forward_reports_outside_beyond_visible_radius` returns Outside for Olympus 14-42 at 14 mm at a content point past f(R_mono), and every visible point inverts within 1e-4 px in at most 32 iterations (`lens_inverse_converges_on_visible_points`).

`warp_reads_bound_never_underestimates_dense_reference`: over 3,000 random windows per named calibration, `reads_radial_rect` contains every densely sampled input coordinate; the corner-only rule is shown underestimating Olympus 14-42 at 14 by more than 30 px.
`focal_beyond_calibrations_refuses_without_extrapolation` and `prime_focal_within_one_percent_snaps_to_calibration` (FC3411 at 8.38 mm uses the 8.4 mm terms; 8.3 mm is refused) hold.

`local_minification_bounds_hold_over_dense_sampling`: the lens closed form and the perspective bound are never below the densely sampled maximum singular value; the Sigma 17-50 at 17 mm reports about 1.732 and the 1:1 double extreme 1.50.

fixtures/geometry/lens-perspective.json holds the named mappings, cover scales, local scales, eight-orientation vectors and alias-energy table; generated read windows are proved in the independent study, and `committed_geometry_fixtures_are_current` passes.

extra_context: New `cargo xtask lensfun-import --source DIR --output DIR` (arm in xtask/src/main.rs, code in new xtask/src/lensfun_import.rs) with a table of the 55 v0.3.4 data/db blob SHA-1s; `import(source, output, expected: &HashMap<&str, &str>)` so tests pass a synthetic table. Admission, exclusion reasons, caps (16 MiB input, 10,000 records whole-import; 256 distortion entries per record excludes the record), keys (`lf1-` + 16 hex of SHA-256 of canonical record JSON), aliases and the lowercase `fixed` mount rule are exactly as the design states.

Core loader in new crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/lens/{mod.rs, index.rs} (mod.rs only declares `pub(crate) mod index; mod pinned;` until the module task): `LensIndex { mounts: Vec<IndexMount>, cameras: Vec<IndexCamera>, lenses: Vec<IndexLens> }`, `IndexLens { key, maker, models, mounts, crop_factor, aspect_ratio, model: DistortionModel, calibrations: Vec<Calibration>, record_sha256 }`, `DistortionModel::{Poly3, Poly5, PtLens}`, `index::resolve_path() -> Option<PathBuf>` (bundle Resources, then beside the executable, then the CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR checkout copy), `index::load_in_background()` (one `rayon::spawn` on the shared pool guarded by a `Once`; no `thread::spawn`, which check-repository's thread-spawn rule forbids here), `index::shared() -> Result<Arc<LensIndex>, Error>` reading a `OnceLock` and never parsing on the caller, and `LensIndex::parse(bytes) -> Result<LensIndex, Error>` checking `pinned::INDEX_SHA256`.

xtask/src/package.rs copies the four data files to Luxforge.app/Contents/Resources/lensfun/ on macOS and lensfun/ beside the executable elsewhere, and the notices inventory lists them as CC-BY-SA-3.0 data. Manual license review stays deferred; do not claim it.
No module, command or control uses the index yet; registration and queries arrive in the module task.

tasks.description: Add warp steps, compile fusion, canonical-order admission, closed-form coverage and the exact reads rule.
extra_context: render/map.rs gains `WarpChain`, `WarpStep::{Affine, Projective, Radial}`, `Projective`, `Radial`, `RadialModel::{Poly3, Poly5, PtLens}` and `MapError::{Outside, Unconverged}` as the design declares; constructors `WarpStep::radial(model, terms, unit_scale, stage)` and `WarpStep::projective(horizontal, vertical, stage)` compute centre, unit, cover, monotone radius and local_scale_max by the closed forms. Constants: `MAX_WARP_STEPS = 3`, `MAX_COVER_SCALE = 4.0`, `MAX_LOCAL_MINIFICATION = 1.8`, `COVER_SAFETY = 1e-12`, `INVERSE_MAX_ITERATIONS = 32`, `INVERSE_TOLERANCE_PX = 1e-4`. One scalar f64 function per step, fixed operation order, no mul_add.

modules/processing.rs: `Processing::Warp(WarpStep)` and `Mapping::Warp(Arc<WarpChain>)`. modules/registry/compile.rs: the fusion rule (first warp opens a segment; a later warp or the crop's affine Resample composes into an open chain with no work after it; an exact integer crop stays exact after the resample), canonical-order refusal with the design's validation message, the 4x cover and 1.8 minification refusals, and `output_stage` for Warp. Identity steps compile to ExactGeometry::identity.

`Mapping::bounds(window) -> Option<(f64, f64, f64, f64)>` carries a continuous box through the chain (corners for affine and projective, the design's candidate points for radial); `Resample::reads` in render/geometry.rs calls it and keeps its single tap floor, so check-repository's one-read-rectangle rule still finds one home.

GeometryMap (render/map.rs) and render/locate.rs evaluate warp segments: to_content by the direct maps, to_output through the bracketed inverse, both returning MapError explicitly; render.transform answers `kind: "warp"` with steps content-to-output, domain, cover {lens, perspective, combined} and local_scale_max.

Tests compile through `#[cfg(test)]` test modules that emit Processing::Warp, because the real modules arrive later. X8: if Detail's host contracts (compile context, Restoration stage, window planner) have landed, rebase onto them; adapt `compile` signatures mechanically.

tasks.description: Answer the Lens section's states from the core: a compatible-only search, a deterministic detected profile, curated camera names and the prefilled missing-lens report.
extra_context: modules/lens/resolve.rs classifies every reason as the photo's or the profile's (`Reason::photo_level`); `search` lists nothing for empty text and, for text, only profiles that fit a matching camera record apart from the photo's reasons, identity matches first; `detect` names the first eligible identity match, else the first held back only by the photo's reasons or its focal length, with the status reasons and the photo's own conditions.

modules/lens/answer.rs builds the whole answer: `state` (applied, already-corrected, camera-not-found, detected, lens-not-found), the lens data (camera_name, product, exif, focal, ledger, reasons, detected) and the query-choice vocabulary (summary, visible_shared, search, current, suggestion with its JPEG `assume-uncorrected` parameters and note, notice, report). Rows carry the same parameters when distortion is unknown and are ineligible with `embedded-distortion-applied` when the source already corrects it.

modules/lens/products.rs is the one curated DJI table (normalized EXIF make and model to product name; display and reports only). modules/lens/report.rs builds the GitHub new-issue URL on the one `NEW_ISSUE_URL` constant: camera, EXIF identity, focal and 35 mm equivalent, crop factor, source kind and interpretation, distortion status, reasons, Lensfun release and commit, Luxforge version; no file name, path, serial or location; one bounded cell per field and at most 6,000 characters.
The control shares only `focal`; the descriptor snapshot is regenerated with its ignored generator.

tasks.description: Extend the query-choice answer vocabulary with host validation and draw it in the desktop: the current and suggested cards, Change, the notice, the report link and per-choice parameters.
extra_context: descriptor/validate.rs `validate_query_choice_answer` checks rows and the optional status vocabulary: cards (`current`, `suggestion`), `notice {level, text}`, `report {label, url}` (https, one token, at most 8,192 bytes), `search`, `visible_shared` (declared shared names) and per-choice `parameters` (declared action parameters other than the key, each valid). docs/design/ui-components.md documents the vocabulary.

state/query_choice.rs parses the vocabulary, `shows_search`, `shows_inputs`, `set_changing` and `suggested`; view/query_choice.rs draws cards, the inline notice, inputs, the search, Retry, the report button and the summary; app/query_choice.rs handles Apply, Change, Report (opened off the update loop through browser.rs, recorded instead by tests and evidence runs) and closes Change after a choice. luxforge-ui gains the pure `inline_notice` widget and its gallery states.

The evidence script gains `query-choice-apply`, `query-choice-change` and `query-choice-report`; xtask/src/lens_smoke.rs drives the detected card, Apply, Change, a compatible search, an empty search and its recorded report, and Close.

tasks.description: Commit a new RAW's eligible detected profile on first open as an ordinary system entry, waiting for the index on the source worker and reporting it on the import job.
extra_context: `ToolModule::first_open` and `ToolModule::await_first_open` are the host's extension point. `EditorService::import_prepared` asks every available, applicable module right after a new asset's Original (`EditorService::first_open` in editor/plan.rs) and commits each proposal through `run_action` by the `system` actor; a re-import, a reopen and an asset with history are never asked. `SourceWork::File` for a file no asset names carries the registry so the source worker awaits readiness after decoding, never the owner.

Lens proposes `select-lens-profile {profile}` only with no lens layer, distortion `known-unapplied` and an eligible detected profile; an unavailable index is an explicit refusal. The import's `job.read` lists `first_open` beside `result`, and `result` and `job.adopt` are the state after the entries.

Harnesses that assumed revision 0 after a RAW import read the imported revision; the RAW journey accepts a first-open entry, and lens qualification measures `before` on the Original; the latency harness resets a RAW baseline's profile.
